NFL Prop Lab

Player prop projections · 12 markets · tested against pre-registered rules · frozen and scored every week

This week

Spread and total are the current consensus from nflverse (not a sportsbook we can price against). Implied points = total ÷ 2 ± spread ÷ 2. Player lines are projected yards: the QB's passing, the lead RB's rushing and the top two WR/TE receiving. Ratings are ranks out of 32 (1 = best), opponent-adjusted EPA per play; pass ratings did not pass their 2025 test, so treat them as rough. Names open the player's profile.

Leaders

Players

Teams

Actual results from nflverse, regular season only. A game counts once its stats are published (about a day after it ends). Team yards and EPA per play cover offensive pass and run plays. Takeaways = interceptions + opponent fumbles recovered. Season views rank points and yards per game.

Projections

Book line / Market over = the sportsbook consensus (most common line across books, and the median over chance with the bookmaker margin removed), collected before games by the weekly run. Model − market is the difference in over chance at that line. It is shown for comparison only: the model has no proven edge over the books yet; a record builds on the Weekly results tab. OUT / DOUBTFUL / Q = the player's final injury report designation, shown once it is published (usually Friday). Projections assume last game's lineup, so skip players marked OUT. Type any number in “Your line” to see the model's chance of going over and under it, from the same 4,000 simulated games. Ranges are the 10th to 90th percentile of 4,000 simulated games. “Over” columns are the model's probability of beating that line, not a sportsbook price. Players need at least 3 earlier games to be projected.

Game simulator

Scores come from the betting spread and total (a normal model of margin and total, which beat a nearest-games model on 2025), linked to the players: when a team's simulated passing volume runs high it tends to be trailing. So this is the market's view of the score, not an independent prediction. Team outcomes can be added to a combination below.

Build a combination

Pick up to three outcomes from this game, including team outcomes (win margin, points, total). The simulator plays the game 1,000 times with the players linked (one pool of pass attempts, QB yards = his receivers' yards) and counts how often all of them happen.

How players in this game move together

Correlation between each QB's passing yards and his receivers' yards across the 1,000 simulated games (0 = unrelated, 1 = always together). Also: correlation between the two teams' pass attempts.

Team ratings

Expected points added (EPA) per play compared with an average team, adjusted for opponents, home field and game situation. Higher is better for every column, defenses included.

Player efficiency ratings

Rating = percentile among qualified players at the position (100 = best). The bar shows the 80% range: a wide bar means the data can't pin this player down yet. Efficiency is opponent-adjusted EPA per dropback (QB), per designed carry (RB) or per target (WR/TE), shrunk toward the position average.

Matchup explorer

How each defense has played, compared with the league. Descriptive only: adding these matchup effects to the projections did not improve forecasts on fresh data, so the projections don't use them.

Each bar is the defense's rate relative to the league (0 = average), shrunk toward average and built only from earlier games. For the offense, longer bars to the right are good news: the defense allows more there.

Defensive scheme profiles

From FTN Data's play charting (2022 on), built only from earlier games and shrunk toward the league. Blitz = share of dropbacks with at least one blitzer. Stacked box = share of designed runs facing 8+ defenders in the box. Play-action and other passes = yards per attempt allowed compared with the league (100 = average; higher = gives up more). Coverage (man/zone) is not shown: that data stops after 2025.

All scores

Show every score for every season, market and model

CRPS and MAE: lower is better. Coverage: share of outcomes inside the 80% interval (target 80%). ECE: average calibration error of over/under probabilities; “noise limit” is the most a perfectly calibrated model would show at that sample size. Bias: average predicted minus actual.

Weekly results

Projections are the ones frozen before the week's first kickoff, never edited afterward. “In range” = the result landed inside the 80% range; about 8 in 10 should. Void = the player did not play (sportsbooks void those props). Surprise = how far the result was from the projection, measured in range widths.

Model health

Live record

Each week's projections are frozen in the ledger before the first kickoff, with a fingerprint of every file, and scored after the games are final and the NFL's stat corrections are in (72 hours after the last game). Rules: phase5/PREREGISTRATION.md.

Data checks from the latest refresh

How this works

  • Every market is built the same way: volume (targets, carries or pass attempts) → successes (catches, completions) → yards drawn from real NFL plays, plus touchdowns and interceptions per play. Each game is simulated 4,000 times.
  • B1 uses a player's own recent averages. B2 uses his share of the team's volume × the team's expected volume from the spread and total.
  • Redistribution re-scales shares when teammates are out so the team still adds up. Opponent adjustment scales efficiency by what the defense allowed to that position. Each is kept only if it improved the 2024 tuning season.
  • QB pass attempts include an “early exit” chance (injury or benching), fit on earlier seasons.

Honest notes

  • Rules for each phase were written and committed before its 2025 test season was scored, and 2025 was scored once. Changes made before scoring are listed as deviations in each phase's PREREGISTRATION.md.
  • Phase 1 (WR/TE): yards passed; receptions improved on the baseline, but not by enough to rule out chance.
  • Phase 3a (10 more markets): none passed. RB rushing yards and attempts beat the baseline by 3–5% but are slightly miscalibrated. Anytime TD improved a little, also slightly miscalibrated. For QB passing, no addition helped, so it stays on the baseline. The shared rushing setup made QB rushing yards worse.
  • Average predictions match reality in every market; the misses are in the shape of the ranges.
  • Watch item: in 2026 weeks 1–5, WR/TE yards ranges covered 75% instead of 80%.
  • Phase 3b (ratings): player ratings beat raw averages at every position on 2025. Team run ratings passed; team pass ratings were better on 2018–2024 but not clearly on 2025.
  • Phase 3c (matchups): run-gap and team-rating features survived development testing by tiny margins (under 0.2%), then made forecasts slightly worse on 2026 and 2025. Depth-of-target, pressure and receiver-archetype features did not survive. Projections therefore stay on the earlier locked models.
  • A data leak was found and fixed during 3c: three league averages used future seasons. All 3c results shown here come from the corrected re-run.
  • Phase 4 (game simulation): linking players in the same game scored 12% better than treating them as independent on 2025 (passed). Its two-outcome probabilities were not clearly better than multiplying on 2025 (they were on 2026 weeks 1–5), and the QB passing-yards check was inconclusive, so the gate did not pass. Single-player projections stay on the earlier models; the simulator is used only for combinations.
  • Phase 6 (defensive scheme): built from FTN Data's play charting (2022 on): blitz rate, stacked boxes against the run, and play-action yards allowed. Only the stacked-box effect on RB rushing yards helped on 2023–2024 (−0.1%), and it did not hold up on 2026 weeks 1–5 or 2025, so projections don't use any of it. Coverage (man/zone) could not be used: that data stops after 2025.
  • Phase 7: using the injury report to guess who plays made projections worse (it added back too many players who did not play), so projections still assume last game's lineup and the injury designation is shown next to each name instead. Weather (wind, cold) helped only 0.08% on 2019–2024, within noise, so it is not used. New markets: RB rushing + receiving yards (3% better than its baseline but ranges slightly narrow), QB completions and receiving TD (no better than the baseline), kicker points (1.7% better than its baseline, ranges slightly wide). None passed every rule.
  • Phase 8 (recalibration): each market's ranges and over/under chances were corrected using how they missed on 2022–2024, then re-tested once on 2025. It is used where it made chances more accurate without hurting overall accuracy: QB passing yards and TDs, anytime TD, receiving TD and kicker points. Anytime TD now passes every rule. For RB rushing it fixed the ranges but made the over/under chances worse, so it is not used there.
  • Phase 9–10 (role changes): when a player's share of snaps jumps or drops, his projected targets and carries now move before his averages catch up. This passed every test (about 0.4–0.6% more accurate) and is used for RB, WR/TE and touchdown markets. WR/TE yards also get a small adjustment when a receiver's yards have lagged how deep he is targeted. A quarterback-change adjustment was tested and did not help, so it is not used.
  • Phase 11 (sharper WR/TE ranges): how spread out a receiver's range is now depends on his volume: a 9-target WR1 and a 3-target WR4 no longer share one shape. When a receiver misses a game, his targets now go mostly to players at his own position. Together these made WR/TE projections about 0.75% more accurate on 2025 and 2026, enough for WR/TE receptions to pass. Recalibration was refit for the other markets with the role signal included.
  • Projections for an unplayed week assume each team's actives from its last game. Check injury news before relying on any number.
  • Nothing here is a betting recommendation. The Tracked picks tab logs picks at US-licensed books as if real money were on them; they become recommendations only after 8+ graded weeks with a return clearly above zero (Phase 12). Bet only where it is legal for you, and only what you can afford to lose.
